findings.reason: §8's codex measurement reads this one field, so a field that cannot read true on the codex arm leaves the treatment arm empty and the verdict unmeasurable.
findings.text: s5 states "the run record's anchored_edit is then true exactly when the key is", but §4 (line 79) defines that field as true only when "the server was registered and Edit and MultiEdit were disallowed in this launch, otherwise false with the reason (unfenced, resumed, operator-settings, no-flight-config)"; on codex neither tool exists to disallow — §8 and s5 both say `apply_patch` cannot be withdrawn — so under §4's predicate the codex arm records false, and §8 splits the population on that recorded fact (line 109), folding every codex anchored run into the baseline arm. The unfenced clause fails the same way: the `-c` overrides do not depend on a fence, so a key-true unfenced codex run registers the server and would record true, which §4 lists as a false reason.

findings.reason: an undeclared dependency lets the coordinator queue s5 beside s4, and the node then fails or fabricates the flag it was told to test.
findings.text: s5's done-when ends "and the flag on the run record", and that record field's writer is named in §4 (line 79) beside `fenced` on the launched-worker record (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2938`, where `"fenced": fenced` is read in the same spec dict), but `plan-section-depends-on` (line 22) declares `"s5":["#s3"]` only, so s5 can be dispatched concurrently with s4 and its own gate then measures a field no landed change writes.

findings.reason: without a named site and its §8 consumer, the codex anchored arm reports zero edits routed through the tool — the same "zero that is an unread field" §1 records as not believable — and §8 cannot tell that zero from a real one.
findings.text: s5 says "the codex stream parser counts edits made through the tool separately from `file_change` items", naming no site, and no parser in the repository reads `mcp_tool_call` at all: the run-record fold in `_CodexDialect.observe` (`reckon/_backends.py:1454-1479`) reads only `thread.started`, `item.completed`/`agent_message`, `rate_limit_event` and `turn.completed`; the shared reads scanner (`reckon/shadow_reads.py:66-122`) reads only `command_execution` and message tool blocks; the edit census that produced §1's codex counts (`docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/worker-anatomy/anatomy_census.py:307-361`) counts `command_execution` and `file_change` only, so an edit routed through `anchored` contributes to neither metric.

findings.reason: substituting pytest's own collectable names (or the project's `python_files`) for the any-language pattern is a one-line change to the deliverable and closes the same defect the section fixes for fixtures; latent today, since no `*.test.py`/`*.spec.py` exists in the tree.
findings.text: s9 narrows the suite command to "files whose name matches the dispatcher's test-file pattern (`_TEST_FILE_RE`) with a `.py` suffix", but that pattern (`reckon/crew/node.py:1013`) admits `*.test.py` and `*.spec.py`, which pytest's collector does not — `pyproject.toml:59` declares no `python_files`, so the default `test_*.py`/`*_test.py` applies — and a scope holding `tests/x.test.py` therefore still hands pytest a file it cannot collect, exits 5, and is refused as `collected_no_test`, the exact failure §9 exists to remove. The rule's stated property ("only the paths pytest collects as tests") is not what the named pattern measures.
